samf-junior-2003-r1-01.title: Multiply by 10
samf-junior-2003-r1-01.body:
Multiplying by $10$ moves the decimal point one place right: $1.1\times10=11$.

**Answer: (B) 11**

samf-junior-2003-r1-03.title: Allowed digits
samf-junior-2003-r1-03.body:
In base $8$ the digits are $0$ to $7$. The number $128$ contains the digit $8$, so it is not valid.

**Answer: (A) 128**

samf-junior-2003-r1-04.title: Subtract
samf-junior-2003-r1-04.body:
Breaking a record means running faster, so subtract: $11.01-0.04=10.97$.

**Answer: (E) 10.97**

samf-junior-2003-r1-05.title: Pattern
samf-junior-2003-r1-05.body:
Powers of $4$ end in $4,6,4,6,\dots$: odd powers end in $4$ and even powers end in $6$. Since $2003$ is odd, the units digit is $4$.

**Answer: (C) 4**

samf-junior-2003-r1-06.title: Opposite faces
samf-junior-2003-r1-06.body:
In the net, the four faces in the row (diamond, cross, open circle, triangle) form a belt around the cube, so the diamond is opposite the open circle and the cross is opposite the triangle. The filled circle and the star are opposite each other.

Opposite faces can never be seen together on the same corner of a cube. Cube B shows the triangle and the cross at the same corner, but they are opposite faces. So B cannot be folded from this net. (The others can: e.g. A shows filled circle, diamond and cross meeting at a corner, which is the situation at the cross in the net.)

**Answer: (B)**

samf-junior-2003-r1-07.title: Use totals
samf-junior-2003-r1-07.body:
An average of $70\%$ of $50$ is $35$ per term, so the four marks add up to $4\times35=140$. From the graph the marks for terms $2,3,4$ are $40,25,45$, which add to $110$. So the first term mark is $140-110=30$ out of $50$, which is $60\%$.

That is between $50\%$ and $70\%$.

**Answer: (E)**

samf-junior-2003-r1-09.title: Fill in the square
samf-junior-2003-r1-09.body:
The square is: top row $x,\ ?,\ 6$; middle row $?,\ 5,\ 1$; bottom row empty.

Third column: $6+1+\text{bottom right}=15$, so the bottom right is $8$. The diagonal from the top left: $x+5+8=15$, so $x=2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

samf-junior-2003-r1-10.title: Use the lcm
samf-junior-2003-r1-10.body:
A number divisible by both $7$ and $8$ is a multiple of $56$. Multiples of $56$ between $800$ and $1000$: $56\times15=840$, $56\times16=896$, $56\times17=952$. ($56\times14=784$ and $56\times18=1008$ are outside.)

That is $3$ numbers.

**Answer: (B) 3**

samf-junior-2003-r1-11.title: Chase the angles
samf-junior-2003-r1-11.body:
Label $P$ on $AB$ and $Q$ on $AC$ as in the figure, with $AP=PQ$. Then $\angle PQA=\angle PAQ=9^\circ$, so the exterior angle $\angle BPQ=18^\circ$.

Next $PQ=QB$, so $\angle QBP=\angle QPB=18^\circ$, and the exterior angle $\angle BQC=9^\circ+18^\circ=27^\circ$ (exterior angle of triangle $AQB$).

The shaded triangle has equal sides $QB=BR$ so its base angles are both $27^\circ$ and its apex angle is $180^\circ-2\times27^\circ=126^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $126^\circ$**

samf-junior-2003-r1-12.title: Telescoping product
samf-junior-2003-r1-12.body:
Each factor is $1-\frac1k=\frac{k-1}k$, so the product is $\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac34\cdots\frac{2002}{2003}$. Every numerator cancels the previous denominator, leaving $\frac1{2003}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac1{2003}$**

samf-junior-2003-r1-13.title: Check each price
samf-junior-2003-r1-13.body:
Nomava has at most R5.20 in total, so R5.40 is impossible.

Her payment is made of $50$c coins and possibly the $20$c coin, so the cents part of the payment is $00$, $20$, $50$ or $70$. The change can only be made of at most two $20$c coins and R1 coins, so its cents part is $00$, $20$ or $40$.

- R1.40 and R4.40 (cents $40$): payment minus price has cents part $60$, $80$, $10$ or $30$. None is allowed.
- R5.10: the only payment of at least R5.10 is R5.20, giving change of $10$c. Not possible.
- R4.60: pay R5.00 (ten $50$c coins); the change is $40$c, two $20$c coins. Possible.

**Answer: (A) R4.60**

samf-junior-2003-r1-14.title: Count pairs of vertices
samf-junior-2003-r1-14.body:
Each vertex joins to $20-3=17$ other vertices by diagonals (not itself and not its two neighbours). That gives $20\times17$ ends, and each diagonal has two ends, so there are $\frac{20\times17}2=170$ diagonals. (Check: for a hexagon, $\frac{6\times3}2=9$.)

**Answer: (C) 170**

samf-junior-2003-r1-14.title: All segments minus sides
samf-junior-2003-r1-14.body:
There are $\binom{20}2=190$ segments joining two vertices; $20$ of them are sides. So $190-20=170$ are diagonals.

**Answer: (C) 170**

samf-junior-2003-r1-15.title: Total distance over total time
samf-junior-2003-r1-15.body:
Going: $120\div60=2$ hours. Returning: $120\div120=1$ hour. Total distance $240$ km, total time $3$ hours, so the average speed is $240\div3=80$ km/h (not the simple average $90$).

**Answer: (E) 80**

samf-junior-2003-r1-16.title: Equations
samf-junior-2003-r1-16.body:
Let there be $a$, $b$, $c$ months at $20$, $16$, $25$ bicycles: $a+b+c=12$ and $20a+16b+25c=213$. Since $213$ is odd, $c$ is odd, and since $c\ge1$, try $c=1,3,5,\dots$.

Subtract $16\times12=192$ from both sides: $4a+9c=21$ (using $b=12-a-c$). Then $c=1$: $4a=12$, $a=3$, $b=8$. ($c=3$ gives $4a=-6$: impossible.)

So $16$ bicycles were sold in $8$ months.

**Answer: (D) 8**

samf-junior-2003-r1-17.title: Volume = area x length
samf-junior-2003-r1-17.body:
In one second $3$ litres $=3000\ \text{cm}^3$ of water pass a point. This is a cylinder of cross-section $250\ \text{cm}^2$ and length $\ell$, so $250\ell=3000$ and $\ell=12$ cm. The water moves $12$ cm each second.

**Answer: (E) 12**

samf-junior-2003-r1-18.title: Use the dimensions
samf-junior-2003-r1-18.body:
Let the edges be $l,b,h$. The face areas are $lh$, $lb$ and $bh$ (in some order), so $ABC=lh\cdot lb\cdot bh=(lbh)^2=V^2$.

**Answer: (C) $V^2$**

samf-junior-2003-r1-19.title: Rewrite
samf-junior-2003-r1-19.body:
$M=\dfrac{10n}{1+2n}=5-\dfrac5{1+2n}$. As $n$ increases, $1+2n$ increases, so $\frac5{1+2n}$ decreases and $M$ increases (getting closer and closer to $5$).

**Answer: (B) increase**

samf-junior-2003-r1-20.title: Two equations
samf-junior-2003-r1-20.body:
Let an egg have $e$ calories and $1$ g of cheese $c$ calories: $4e+60c=560$ and $6e+20c=560$. Multiply the second by $3$: $18e+60c=1680$. Subtract the first: $14e=1120$, so $e=80$.

**Answer: (C) 80**
